questions.q: What is the standard order of operations inside a typical CNN 'conv block'?
options: Pooling, then convolution, then dropout
Convolution, then batch normalization, then a nonlinearity, often followed by pooling
Linear layer, then convolution, then softmax
Flatten, then convolution, then batch normalization
questions.explain: The standard repeating unit is conv -> batch norm -> activation (commonly ReLU) -> optional pooling, stacked repeatedly to build depth.

questions.q: As a CNN's conv blocks go deeper, what typically happens to channel count and spatial resolution?
options: Both increase together
Both decrease together
Channel count typically increases while spatial resolution typically decreases (via pooling or strided convolutions)
Channel count and spatial resolution never change inside a CNN
questions.explain: Deeper blocks commonly increase the number of channels (richer learned features) while pooling or strided convolutions shrink the spatial size, trading detail for abstraction.

questions.q: For a 32x32 input passed through two `nn.MaxPool2d(2)` layers (with convolutions that preserve spatial size via padding), what is the resulting spatial size?
questions.explain: Each MaxPool2d(2) halves the spatial dimensions: 32 -> 16 after the first, 16 -> 8 after the second, matching the 8x8 feature map used in this lesson's classifier input size.

questions.q: What does `torch.flatten(x, 1)` do to a tensor of shape `(batch, 64, 8, 8)`?
options: Collapses every dimension including the batch dimension into one long vector
Collapses dimensions from index 1 onward into one, producing shape (batch, 64*8*8), while leaving the batch dimension untouched
Removes the channel dimension entirely
Adds a new dimension at index 1
questions.explain: The second argument to torch.flatten specifies the first dimension to start flattening from; passing 1 preserves dimension 0 (the batch) and merges everything after it into a single dimension.

questions.q: In `nn.Linear(64 * 8 * 8, num_classes)` following the feature extractor in this lesson, why is the input size `64 * 8 * 8`?
options: It is an arbitrary number unrelated to the feature extractor
It matches the flattened size of the (64, 8, 8) feature map produced by the convolutional blocks before this layer
It is the number of classes squared
It represents the batch size used during training
questions.explain: The classifier's input dimension must match the flattened feature map it receives — here, 64 channels of 8x8 spatial size, flattened to 64*8*8 features per sample.
